summary: monogrok is an obfuscated bulk-email / phishing delivery toolkit that disables TLS verification process-wide
details: monogrok ships as ~100 heavily obfuscated JavaScript files (string-array obfuscation with `_0x` symbol names across commands/, functions/, utils/) implementing a bulk-email and phishing operator toolkit. The advertised feature set (per _init/.monotomic.help.txt and the commands/index.js dispatcher) includes SOCKS5 proxy rotation, recipient-MX direct delivery to bypass mail relays, 50 message-body encryption/encoding presets, 50 attachment scripter presets, 75 link-obfuscation/redirect presets, attachment-extension spoofing (e.g. deliver `Attachment-1.html` as `Invoice.pdf`, `.exe`→`.pdf`, `.msi`/`.7z`/`.rar` allowed), zero-font body letter injection, and bulk from-address rotation — i.e. mass-phishing infrastructure with anti-detection presets. On top of that, denv.js is required at the top of ultra.js (the package `main` and `bin` target) and unconditionally sets `process.env.NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED='0'`, which silently turns off TLS certificate verification for the entire Node process. Any application that loads monogrok loses TLS validation for every other HTTPS client in the same process, weakening MITM resistance throughout the host program. functions/globals.js additionally POSTs to `https://api.mntmc.rip/pqZXDFG345i/potus?email=<user.email>` with operator activity payloads, which is author-controlled telemetry tied to the licensed operator account. The combination of (a) pervasive obfuscation of every code file, (b) process-wide TLS-verification disable on module load, and (c) shipped abuse infrastructure designed to deliver disguised payloads via spoofed attachments through arbitrary MX servers makes this package unsafe to install in any developer or build environment.
